audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate strings claim Winds of War heals Galio: spikes[0].text ("a long-range tornado that chunks you and heals him"), early ("pokes you from range and heals him"), and wants.you[0] ("Dodge Winds of War (Q) to deny poke and heal"). Galio's Q does not heal.
audit.why: Riot's Winds of War text is "Galio fires two windblasts that converge into a large tornado that deals damage over time" — no healing. Galio has no healing anywhere in his kit; not one of his five abilities carries a heal flag. This is a fabricated sustain source repeated three times, and it changes how a player values the poke war: it tells them Galio profits from every tornado when in fact chip he lands costs him nothing and gains him nothing back.
audit.corrected: Removed the heal from all three strings and replaced it with the real detail — 825 range and the Colossal Smash passive.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (Winds of War; no heal flag on any ability)

audit.whatIsWrong: The layers disagree on five of seven stages. content.win reads Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio/Skill/Zac; full.phases sides read Skill/Zac/Zac/Skill/Skill/Zac/Zac. The full layer hands Zac levels 2 and 3 outright in a lane he loses.
audit.why: Zac wins 48.26% over 230 games — this is his losing matchup, and the content layer chart reflects that while the full layer does not. A player opening the full-layer chart is told they win levels 2 and 3 against a champion who out-ranges them 825 to 800 and has a point-and-click-tier taunt.
audit.corrected: Aligned full.phases sides to the content chart: Galio through level 6, Skill at first item, Zac at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire entry is built around tracking Justice Punch — tldr, focus, breakdown.cooldowns and four phase texts all name it as the cooldown to punish. Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7s.
audit.why: An 11-second cooldown at rank 1 is not a punish window; it is back before Zac can cross the lane and re-engage. The cooldown that actually decides whether a Zac commit survives is Shield of Durand at 18/17/16/15/14s, because the taunt is what turns his engage into a free trade for Galio. Building the matchup metronome on the short cooldown instead of the long one is the substantive error.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed breakdown.cooldowns at Shield of Durand at 18s, noted Justice Punch is only 11s and not worth waiting on, added Hero's Entrance at 180s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that Justice Punch begins with a backward step.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters." The backstep moves him out of the spot a Zac Q was aimed at, so a Galio who presses E in response to Stretching Strikes can both dodge the grab and answer with a knockup. It also means his effective threat range is longer than the 650 listed.
audit.corrected: Noted the backstep and that it can dodge Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] pairs "Pick up every blob" with "Galio wastes Justice Punch — commit the full pattern immediately", and dontsFull[1] pairs "Let him stomp blobs" with "Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown".
audit.why: The same generator template mismatch present in the Darius and Fiora entries — titles and bodies describe different things.

edits.before: Galio out-pokes you early: Winds of War (Q) is a long-range tornado that chunks you and heals him, and his passive on-hit magic burst punishes any melee trade, so respect Q spacing.
edits.after: Galio out-pokes you early: Winds of War (Q) is an 825-range tornado that grinds you down over time, and his Colossal Smash passive burst punishes any melee step-up, so respect Q spacing.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are Galio's: Winds of War (Q) pokes you from range and heals him while his passive burst punishes any melee step-up, so give ground and farm at max range.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are Galio's: Winds of War (Q) pokes you from 825 range while his Colossal Smash passive punishes any melee step-up, so give ground and farm at max range.

edits.before: Dodge Winds of War (Q) to deny poke and heal
edits.after: Sidestep Winds of War (Q) to deny his poke

edits.before: Justice Punch (E) knockup into Shield of Durand (W) taunt is a hard lockdown combo, and Hero's Entrance (R) lets him gank other lanes — his level-6 CC threat is real, though his solo kill pressure on you is low.
edits.after: Justice Punch (E) knockup into Shield of Durand (W) taunt is hard lockdown, and his E steps back before charging, which can dodge your Q — bait both before you engage. His solo kill pressure stays low.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Galio's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Justice Punch into Shield of Durand is his lockdown, and Hero's Entrance lets him decide another lane while you are stuck holding this one.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Galio Shield of Durand: 18s at rank 1 — the taunt is what punishes your commit, so it matters far more than his dash. - Justice Punch: only 11s, it is back fast, never build a window on it. - Hero's Entrance: 180s.

edits.before: Galio wastes Justice Punch — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Blobs are your sustain and your revive margin — trade along them.

notes: Biggest correction in this slice: Winds of War was described as healing Galio in three separate strings (spikes[0].text, early, wants.you[0]). Galio has no healing on any ability — this is invented sustain, and it makes the poke war read backwards for the player. Worth grepping other files for the same claim, since the phrasing differs each time and looks generated rather than copy-pasted. Second structural problem: the full layer awarded Zac levels 2 and 3 in a lane he loses at 48.26% over 230 games, contradicting the content layer's chart; I aligned the full layer to the content layer rather than the other way round because the content chart matches the data. Third: the entry's whole spine is "track Justice Punch", which is an 11s cooldown at rank 1 — too short to plan around. The taunt on Shield of Durand at 18s is the real gate on a Zac engage, so I re-pointed breakdown.cooldowns; note that tldr and focus still name Justice Punch and would need the same treatment, but they sit outside what one length-banded edit can sensibly carry. Not asserted: whether Justice Punch's knockup interrupts Zac's Elastic Slingshot wind-up. That is very likely and high-elo Galio players play for it, but interrupt behaviour on charged abilities is exactly what the kit file marks unknown, so I left it out rather than guess.
